newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU MULLS CASH ADVANCE FOR FLOOD-HIT GERMAN FARMS.
newsitem.headline: EU MULLS CASH ADVANCE FOR FLOOD-HIT GERMAN FARMS.

text.p: The European Union will vote on Thursday on emergency moves to unblock cash for flood-hit east German farmers, EU farm officials said on Monday.

Autumn farm support payments will be paid out early to farmers in the eastern German state of Brandenburg if a majority of the EU's cereals management committee backs the plan drawn up by the European Commission.
The committee, comprising experts from the EU's 15 member states, is expected to accept the plan, officials said.
German farm minister Jochen Borchert asked for the help in late July as the worst flooding in living memory started ruining tracts of farmland and wrecking villages.

Total damage has yet to be calculated, but officials say it could run into billions of marks. Germany has, however, escaped the worst of the floods, which killed more than 100 people in the neighbouring Czech Republic and Poland.
EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler has already told affected farmers they can graze cattle on set-aside land -- fields left idle to limit production -- if they run out of feed.
Autumn farm payments, usually only available from October, are around $58 per hectare for grain farmers and $100 per hectare for oilseed farmers.
Around 40,000 hectares of crop or grazing land in eastern Germany were swamped by the floods.
